questions.q: What file extension does every Solidity file need to end in?
questions.explain: Every Solidity file must end in .sol — that's how Remix (and the compiler) knows it's a Solidity file.

questions.q: What real rule of thumb did the instructor give for choosing a pragma version?
options: Use the latest version available, not the oldest, since older versions carry bugs that were later fixed
Always use the very first version, 0.4
Use a random version each time
The version number doesn't matter at all
questions.explain: The instructor explicitly recommended using the latest available compiler version, since older versions have known bugs that later releases fixed.

questions.q: What happens if you leave off the semicolon after the pragma line in Remix?
options: The contract deploys anyway with a warning
It automatically adds one for you silently
Nothing — semicolons are always optional in Solidity
Remix shows a real compiler error
questions.explain: The instructor demonstrated live that removing the semicolon produces a visible error in Remix — it's a required part of the line.

questions.q: In `string message = "Hello class";`, what does the word `string` represent?
options: The data type — indicating the variable holds a word or collection of letters
questions.explain: `string` is the data type declaration. `message` is the variable's name, and `"Hello class"` is its actual value.

questions.q: Which of these is a valid single-line comment in Solidity, per this lesson?
questions.explain: Solidity uses two forward slashes (//) for a single-line comment, and /* ... */ for a multi-line comment — both are ignored by the compiler.
